Trace, implement and test: 03.05.Sort of Stacks

Study exercise derived from this source. Explain the approach in your own words, work through an example, and identify edge cases. For code, implement your own version and discuss its time and space complexity.

Original source context
class SortedStack {
public:
    SortedStack() {
    }

    void push(int val) {
        stack<int> t;
        while (!stk.empty() && stk.top() < val) {
            t.push(stk.top());
            stk.pop();
        }
        stk.push(val);
        while (!t.empty()) {
            stk.push(t.top());
            t.pop();
        }
    }

    void pop() {
        if (!isEmpty()) {
            stk.pop();
        }
    }

    int peek() {
        return isEmpty() ? -1 : stk.top();
    }

    bool isEmpty() {
        return stk.empty();
    }

private:
    stack<int> stk;
};

/**
 * Your SortedStack object will be instantiated and called as such:
 * SortedStack* obj = new SortedStack();
 * obj->push(val);
 * obj->pop();
 * int param_3 = obj->peek();
 * bool param_4 = obj->isEmpty();
 */
